subject: Pricing follow-up: Target $/1M tokens & benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Subject: Follow-up & target $/1M tokens (recap from today)

Hi Samantha / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today — helpful to walk through your ingestion and routing flow. Quick recap and next steps from our side.

Recap (call notes):
- Estimated production inference volume: ~40M tokens/month initially, ramp to ~150M over Q1 next year.
- Workloads: short-chat + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for support assistants; average response length ~150 tokens.
- SLO: p99 latency target ~600ms; need predictable unit economics.
- Compliance: SOC 2 in scope, customer-managed KMS for private deployment under consideration.

Budget / target price you mentioned: aim for ~$20 / 1M tokens as a goal for unit cost (target priced benchmarking). You asked for a comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic and hosted open-model providers, plus a concrete pricing sheet for Redwood (hosted vs dedicated).

Next steps I committed to:
1) Share a short pricing benchmarking note (attached) showing $/1M tokens across OpenAI, Anthropic, and typical hosted open-model providers, plus Redwood target ranges.
2) Share a tailored pricing sheet for Acme with volume tiers and reserved (Dedicated) pricing.
3) Follow up with SOC 2 evidence and SSO/KMS notes.

I attached an initial volume estimate spreadsheet you shared in the call (acme-volume-estimate.xlsx) and our pricing sheet (redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf).

If anything in the recap is off, flag it and I’ll correct. Proposed follow-up: 30-min call next Tuesday 11/23 to go over the pricing scenarios and procurement steps.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks for the recap and the attachments — helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before the follow-up call:

1) Volume confirmation: the 40M tokens/month is our conservative starting point. If PoC looks good, we expect to scale to ~120–150M over three months.
2) Budget: our procurement team set an internal target of $500–$800/month for the PoC, which aligns with your note about target $/1M tokens — right now our math implies a desired effective price of ~$12–$20 / 1M tokens at 40M tokens/month.

Appreciate the quick turn.

—Samantha

Subject: Re: Follow-up & target $/1M tokens (recap from today)

Samantha —

Great — thanks for the specifics. See inline answers and a short benchmarking summary below.

Volume/discounts
- For 40M tokens/month: Redwood hosted (open-model self-hosted variants) list pricing: $9 / 1M tokens.
- With a 12-month reserved (Dedicated) commit at that volume, we can provide a discounted rate of $6 / 1M tokens (tiered commit).
- If you hit 120–150M tokens/month, the committed tier improves to $4.5–$5.5 / 1M tokens depending on burst allowances and model selection.

Benchmarking vs common providers (approximate $ / 1M tokens for comparable generation workloads):
- OpenAI (GPT-4 family, hosted): ~$120 / 1M tokens (high variability depending on prompt/completion split and GPT variant).
- Anthropic (Claude 2/3 hosted): ~$80 / 1M tokens.
- Hosted open-model providers (Replicate, some managed hosts): typically $25–$60 / 1M tokens depending on model and optimizations (quantized vs fp16).
- Redwood (hosted open-model): $9 / 1M tokens (list) — Dedicated commit pricing can get down to $4.5–$6 / 1M tokens at scale.

Why the gap? Unit economics example (simplified):
- Open models (quantized, optimized inference) can run 4–8x cheaper on GPU util than large proprietary models due to smaller memory footprint, continuous batching, and KV cache reuse.
- Proprietary models (e.g., GPT-4) have licensing and model costs plus higher compute per token, which is why list $/1M tokens is materially higher.

Tailored PoC scenario (your 40M/month target):
- Redwood hosted (no commit): $9 / 1M => monthly: ~$360.
- Redwood Dedicated 12-mo (committed): $6 / 1M => monthly: ~$240.
- Target you mentioned ($12–$20 / 1M): our hosted list at $9 already meets the lower bound; with commitment we can beat your target to $6.

Compliance & next steps
- SOC 2: we have current SOC 2 Type II report; I’ll send a link to the secure evidence (or we can provide redacted report under NDA).
- KMS: Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS; we’ll include the KMS integration note in the procurement packet.

Attachments & links
- Attached: redwood-pricing-sheet.pdf (detailed tiers) and a notes page with the benchmarking snapshot.
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/7842
- DocuSign (SOW stub): https://www.docusign.com/ABC-123

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-minute call to review pricing scenarios and procurement ask — can you confirm availability for Tue 11/23?
2) I’ll share SOC 2 evidence and a dedicated SKU/quote for the 12-month commit for your procurement team to review.
3) If agreed, we’ll issue a draft SOW + DocuSign for signature and spin up a Dedicated trial slot for baseline latency testing.

If you want, I can also pull a very small test invoice showing the committed vs uncommitted delta so procurement can see the monthly savings.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
